title: Packing response
description: The packing plan: which physical boxes to use, and where every unit sits inside them. Positions are the corner nearest the origin, and sizes are AS PLACED with rotation already applied, so a consumer can render each placement as a cuboid with no further maths.

status.description: solved: every unit placed. partial: some placed, some not. rejected: nothing placed. Derived from unpacked and containers, never set independently.

containers.description: One entry per PHYSICAL box used. Two uses of the same box type appear as two entries.

unpacked.description: Units that could not be placed, each with a machine-readable reason. Empty when status is solved.

warnings.description: Non-fatal notes for humans, for example a keepTogether preference the solver had to break.

position.description: Corner of the item nearest the origin, in millimetres. Origin is the inside bottom-left-back corner of the box. Never a centre point.

instanceId.description: Unique per physical box in this response, for example B-SMALL#1 and B-SMALL#2.

boxId.description: The box type from the request this was drawn from.

name.description: Box type's human label, copied through.

interior.description: Copied from the box type. Repeated here so a consumer can render a container without cross-referencing the request.

step.description: GLOBAL 1-based pack order across the whole response, not per container. Sort every placement by step and reveal one at a time to drive the step-by-step view.

itemId.description: The item line from the request.

unit.description: Which unit of that line this is, 1-based. A line with quantity 3 produces units 1, 2 and 3.

reference.description: SKU, copied through for display and scanning.

size.description: Dimensions AS PLACED, with rotation already applied. Draw a cuboid of this size at position and you are done. This will differ from the request size when rotation is not WHD.

rotation.description: How the item's original width, height and depth map onto the placed x, y and z axes. WHD is unrotated. Informational only: size already reflects it, so a renderer can ignore this field.

reason.description: NO_BOX_FITS: larger than the interior of every box type. INCOMPATIBLE: group rules bar it from every box it could have shared. EXCEEDS_WEIGHT: fits by volume but would breach a weight limit.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation for the portal to surface to a packer.

utilisation.description: How full this container is. Volumes in cubic millimetres, weights in grams.

weightUsed.description: Gross: contents plus the box's own tare weight.

solveTimeMs.description: Wall-clock time inside the solver. The client's bar is 1000 to 2000 ms for a single order.

volumeUtilisation.description: Across all containers. Our headline efficiency number.

algorithm.description: Which strategy produced this, for example first-fit-decreasing. Lets us compare approaches on the same input.
